:::{#exm-nb-reg}
#### Negative binomial variance

Suppose a negative binomial regression model (@def-nb-reg)
has $\rho = 2$,
and that at some covariate pattern and exposure
the mean count is $\mu(\vx, t) = 4$.
By @eq-nb-reg-var:

$$
\ba
\Var{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t}
&= 4 + \frac{4^2}{2}
&& \text{(substitute } \mu = 4 \text{ and } \rho = 2 \text{)} \\
&= 4 + 8
&& \text{(square and divide)} \\
&= 12
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

A Poisson regression model with the same mean
would specify variance $4$,
so this negative binomial model allows three times as much variance at this mean.
At a covariate pattern with mean $\mu(\vx, t) = 1$,
the same model gives variance $1 + 1^2 / 2 = 1.5$,
only $1.5$ times the Poisson variance:
the extra variance $\mu^2 / \rho$ grows faster than the mean,
so negative binomial overdispersion is largest where counts are large.
As $\rho \to \infty$,
$\mu^2 / \rho \to 0$
and the variance approaches the Poisson variance $\mu$.

:::
